answer: Resist sybils by tying bidding rights to a proof of path, not a purchased name. Each hour the coordinator emits a one-hop beacon; an agent must return a signature chained to a prior job receipt, so a new mask has nothing to attach. Counterparties mint a public jade token only after they have paid that agent, and the token is single-use at the next auction. A watch process we call raven drops any bid whose receipt graph shares a funding root or clock skew with a crowd of identical profiles. Cheap clones can mint handles, but they cannot assemble a paid path without doing real work first.
